prerequisites: Basic notions acquired in previous Physics and Mathematics courses
Ability for abstraction, basic calculation, and information synthesis
Skills for group work and group communication

learning_outcomes.text: Knowledge in basic and technological subjects that enables them to learn new methods and theories, and provides them with versatility to adapt to new situations.
Understanding and mastery of basic concepts about the general laws of mechanics, thermodynamics, fields and waves, and electromagnetism, as well as their application to solving engineering problems.
Understand the basic concepts about the general laws of electromagnetism and thermodynamics.
Know the basic instrumentation for measuring physical quantities.
Know the basic techniques for evaluating experimental data.
Develop practical solutions to elementary technical engineering problems in the fields of electromagnetism and thermodynamics.

syllabus_topics: 4.2.- Capacitors in series and in parallel.
4.3.- Energy storage in capacitors and electric field energy.
4.4.- Dielectrics, molecular model of induced charge and polarization vector.
5.5.- Energy and power in electrical circuits.
6.2.- Motion of a charged particle in a magnetic field.
6.3.- Magnetic force on a current-carrying conductor.
6.4.- Force and torque on a current loop.
6.6.- Magnetic field lines and magnetic flux.
9.3.- State variables and state of a system.
9.6.- Change of state, transformation or process.
10.1.- Thermal equilibrium, zeroth principle and temperature.
10.3.- Ideal gas thermometer and the Kelvin scale.
11.5.- Internal energy of the ideal gas.
11.6.- Molar heat capacity of the ideal gas.
11.7.- Adiabatic, isothermal, isobaric and isochoric processes for the ideal gas.
12.2.- Heat engines, refrigeration machines and heat pumps.
12.3.- Second principle of thermodynamics: Clausius and Kelvin-Planck statements.
12.8.- Principle of increasing entropy of the universe.
Practices related to classroom content will be carried out, which may include:
1.- Use of the multimeter. Ohm's Law. Direct current. Circuit with resistors.
3.- Charging and discharging of a capacitor.
4.- Study of the parallel plate capacitor with dielectrics.
5.- Use of the oscilloscope to visualize charging and discharging processes.
6.- Study of the magnetic field. Helmholtz coils, magnetic moment. Hall effect.
7.- Calorimetry. Water equivalent of the calorimeter. Latent heat of fusion.
8.- Thermodynamics of the ideal gas. Adiabatic index. Adiabatic work.

Optional activities: Sessions with unstructured activities (open practice) covering the theoretical content of the practices listed above. Student groups must solve a practical problem proposed by the professor, selecting the theoretical framework and experimental tools to obtain the solution; for this, they will have basic information and professor guidance.

assessment_methods.method: Practical reports, practicum and external internships

assessment_rules: The final grade G for continuous evaluation is calculated as C (40%) + F (40%) + L (20%), where C, F, and L are the most recent grades for classroom content (course and final tests) and laboratory, respectively. For global evaluation, applicable to students with a waiver for continuous assessment, the final grade G is A (80%) + L (20%), where A is the most recent classroom grade and L is the most recent laboratory grade. To obtain a laboratory grade L0 in the ordinary opportunity, attendance at all laboratory sessions is mandatory; otherwise, L0 = 0.0. A final grade of 5.0 or higher (on a 0-10 scale) is required to pass the course. Any unethical behavior (copying, plagiarism, unauthorized electronic devices) will result in a final grade of 0.0 for that assessment opportunity.
